newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Moroccan court sentences "boycott election" group.
newsitem.headline: Moroccan court sentences "boycott election" group.

text.p: A Moroccan court on Tuesday gave suspended three-month jail terms to four activists of the Avant-Garde Democratic and Socialist Party (PADS) arrested for calling for a boycott of local elections earlier this month.

The Moroccan news agency MAP said the four, who were also each fined 1,500 dirhams ($160), were charged with spreading slanderous information and distributing tracts urging disobedience and a boycott of the June 13 elections.

The court, in the city of Fes, acquitted 18 others held on the same charges. Four of them belonged to a fundamentalist movement called the Addawa Wal Tabligh and were distributing tracts charging that the Moroccan political parties and parliament were illegal according to the Moslem religion, the agency said.

Earlier this month, in a statement sent to local media, PADS said a total of 125 activists, including a woman, were arrested in more than 26 provinces throughout the country recently for their boycott campaign.
Among Morocco's dozen active parties, PADS was the only opposition group to call for the boycott of local elections.
